text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/frontend-release-design-sol.md <<'EOF'
# Selective release design

Keep one release workflow and one shared build action. Introduce a small, offline-testable release-planning script and one optional action input `build-backend` (boolean string, default `true`). The app continues to build for every triggered push, including backend-only pushes, because its footer embeds the newly allocated version. Backend build steps run only when the plan requires them. Manual release dispatch and ARM dispatch omit the new input and therefore retain all four builds.

## Organizing shape and ownership

The planner owns a single complete plan:

```json
{
  "buildBackend": false,
  "baseline": {"version": "2026.10.26.12.00", "source": "FULL_SHA"},
  "backend": {
    "server": "ghcr.io/owner/repo@sha256:...",
    "migrate": "ghcr.io/owner/repo@sha256:...",
    "cli": "ghcr.io/owner/repo@sha256:..."
  }
}
```

For a full build, `buildBackend` is true and baseline/backend are null. Do not allow partially reusable backend sets. Plan fields provide action input/output plumbing; the existing four-key `amd64.json` remains the build artifact. Merge freshly built app digest with either three built backend digests or three validated carried references. Keep final `images.json` schema unchanged: current version and source plus all four immutable references. Clarify documentation that top-level source identifies release contents while carried backend OCI labels retain their original build source.

`prepare` checks out full history, fetches published release metadata and its `images.json`, invokes the planner, and supplies backend selection plus carried values to `build`. `build` passes `build-backend` into the action, constructs a complete artifact, and release tagging stays the same four-variant loop. Validate complete artifact before making any tags. Never rebuild or flatten carried backend indexes: copy the original digest references, preserving attestations and exact digest identity. `image.txt` and floating server alias use carried server reference when appropriate.

## Baseline and safety

Compare the current tree to a successfully published release's manifest `source`, never the last push, a reserved tag, a partial registry tag, or a previous workflow attempt. Resolve published non-draft/non-prerelease release metadata, use its attached manifest, validate repository refs, full source SHA, version/release correspondence, required four keys and sha256 digest syntax, then require baseline source to be an ancestor of current SHA. First release, absent/invalid manifest, metadata download/API failures or nonancestor baseline select full build. Do not interpret failures as an empty diff.

Conservative smallest classifier: backend reuse is permitted only when every changed path is under `frontend/` or exactly `docker/Dockerfile.frontend`; any other change forces full build. This fails safely for future root inputs, build-action changes, Docker ignore changes and release script edits, without maintaining a growing backend dependency allowlist. Use NUL-delimited paths and include deletion/rename sides. Documentation-only commits since the baseline may cause extra full builds, an acceptable conservative tradeoff.

Overlapping releases need not share mutable baseline state: capture the selected published manifest once in prepare and carry it through the run. If a newer published source is not an ancestor, full-build fallback preserves correctness. Existing concurrent release ordering of Latest/server alias is a separate issue; do not expand this change into release serialization unless required.

## Cache isolation

Use `exposed-backend-linux-${architecture}` for all three backend targets and `exposed-frontend-linux-${architecture}` for app, for both cache reads and writes. All backend targets share their scope and builder as today. Remove shared frontend/backend fallback reads; avoid perpetuating cache contention through the old mixed architecture/multiarch scopes. Initial cold cache is acceptable and must not affect selection correctness. Manual runs warm both new scopes; ARM gets distinct architecture scopes automatically.

## Alternatives

Split frontend/backend producer workflows plus a coordinating release workflow could isolate build schedules structurally, but requires cross-workflow artifact selection, release source/version coordination, asynchronous failure handling and another immutable manifest boundary. Separate backend/app jobs within this workflow is viable but duplicates setup and loses the current simple sequential shared action. Conditional steps in the existing action plus a single explicit plan gives the smallest change while ensuring backend work is absent, independently of cache behavior.

## Behavioral checks

Use temporary Git repositories and fixture release metadata/manifests to exercise the planner: frontend only; frontend Dockerfile only; mixed changes; backend changes missed by an intervening failed push; migrations, lockfile, SQLx, Docker ignore, shared action and planner changes; first release; malformed/missing keys/digest/source/version; metadata network failure; unrelated/newer baseline; deleted/renamed backend paths. Assert expected backend decision and preserved references, not merely matched strings.

Exercise artifact assembly with fake digests and assert all four immutable references and source/version, and byte-identical carried backend digests. Stub build/publish interfaces to demonstrate app-only calls omit all three backend targets, all-build calls include them, and release copying receives every variant; failure before complete artifact never publishes partial metadata. Validate workflow/action syntax and default input behavior for manual AMD64 and ARM. A real frontend-only release confirms no backend steps execute, all four version tags resolve to manifest references, carried refs retain their attestation indexes, and the app reports the new version.
EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));

content.text:
Created design at `/tmp/frontend-release-design-sol.md`.

Recommendation: retain one workflow with conditional backend steps, a validated published-release baseline, conservative frontend-only classification, complete unchanged manifests, and isolated cache scopes. Includes alternatives and behavioral verification strategy.
